Recording summary

At the start of the unit, the agent identified split K/V streams as a likely bandwidth cost at long context and proposed packing the values at each sequence position:

> “128k is still bandwidth-bound on split K/V streams. I’ll pack K and V per position so each step is one sequential 512-byte read.”

The edits changed the cache write to store K followed by V for each [kv_head, position], and changed attention reads to derive both pointers from the packed position address. Cache allocation became:

# Packed [kv, seq, 2, hd] so K and V at a position are 512B sequential.
# Both lists alias the same storage; the kernel reads k_cache as packed.
packed = [
    torch.zeros(NUM_KV, max_seq, 2, HEAD_DIM, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    for _ in range(num_layers)
]
return packed, packed

The kernel’s write path likewise stored both vectors at that position:

// packed [NKV, max_seq, 2, HD] — K then V at each position
__nv_bfloat16* kvw = k_cache_w + ((size_t)kv_h * max_seq + pos) * (2 * HD);
for (int i = tid; i < HD; i += BLOCK) {
    kvw[i] = __float2bfloat16(sk[i]);
    kvw[HD + i] = __float2bfloat16(sv[i]);
}

Memory summary

grok-4.6 implemented the four-layer Qwen3-0.6B decode path in real CUDA. The official result passed correctness and received a score of 0.0542, ranking 8th of 20 scored runs on the RTX PRO 6000. CUDA graph replay captures one decode step and replays it across steps when capture succeeds. A pointer signature controls graph reuse; otherwise the implementation falls back to an eager loop.

The final cache layout stores K and V together as [kv, seq, 2, hd], making them contiguous for each position. Earlier attempts at L2 persistence, weight packing, and graph capture hit compile, runtime, or capture errors. Removing the persistence and weight-packing path and using private-stream graph capture resolved those issues.
